newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso ends firm as dollars flood market.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso ends firm as dollars flood market.

text.p: Colombia's peso was driven up by a flood of greenbacks into the market and closed up 1.1 pesos at 1,007.1 pesos per dollar, its highest level since January 11, interbank traders said.
"The dollar could have fallen further had it not been for banks snapping up greenbacks to help buoy the month-end peso-dollar exchange rate calculation," one interbank trader said.
She added that the central bank had intervened in the market to break the dollar's fall at 1,006.2 pesos.
"Dollars are flooding the markets," one trader said, who explained there was little client demand.
"Companies already bought dollars to pay their bills abroad at the start of the year and there is no real demand for greenbacks however attractive the price seems," the dealer added.

Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Monday he would ask the central bank's board of directors to take a stronger hand in the foreign exchange markets in an effort to control the excessive supply of dollars in the short term.
Interbank traders reported 333 trades worth a total $131 million.
The peso hit an intra-day high of 1,005.7 pesos per dollar and an intra-day low of 1,008.5 pesos, averaging out at 1,007.35 during the session.
